statement: A ball is thrown upward from a balcony. Its height above the ground, in feet, $t$ seconds after it is thrown is $h(t) = -16t^2 + 64t + 5$. What is the maximum height, in feet, that the ball reaches?

choices.misconception: I found the time when the ball is highest, t = 2 seconds, and gave that instead of the height.
I used t = -b/a = 4 for the vertex instead of -b/(2a), and h(4) = 5, which is just the starting height again.
I found the right time, t = 2, but forgot to add the starting height of 5 feet, so I got 64.

hints: The highest point of a parabola that opens downward is its vertex.
The vertex is at $t = -\frac{b}{2a}$. Find that time, then substitute it into $h(t)$.

solutions.elegant: Complete the square: $h(t) = -16(t^2 - 4t) + 5 = -16(t - 2)^2 + 64 + 5$. The term $-16(t - 2)^2$ is never positive, so the largest height is $69$ feet.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
